---
title: TfModule Demo
---

# TfModule

A `<TfModule>` block draws its form from an OpenTofu module and generates the code that uses it. The module's `variables.tf` gives each input's name, type, default and validation; its `runbook_block.yml` says how to present them. A `<GitHubPullRequest>` block then pushes that code, and a `<TerragruntApply>` block applies it.

This runbook uses a copy of the `google-group` module from the catalog. The module's `runbook_block.yml` declares the lookups behind the organization dropdown and the people suggestions, and the `auth` prop binds them to the `<GoogleAuth>` block below, which sends them as the person who signs in. Until someone does, those fields say so, and take typed values.

## Sign in to Google Workspace

<GoogleAuth
  id="workspace"
  scopes={[
    "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform",
    "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/userinfo.email",
    "openid",
    "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/admin.directory.customer.readonly",
    "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/admin.directory.domain.readonly",
    "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/admin.directory.user.readonly",
  ]}
/>

## Clone your infrastructure repository

<GitHubAuth id="github" />

<GitClone id="infra-live" githubAuthId="github" title="Clone your infrastructure repository" />

## Describe the group

<TfModule
  id="group"
  source="google-group"
  template="templates/google-group-unit"
  path="google-groups/{{ .id }}"
  auth={{ google: "workspace" }}
/>

The runbook decides how to use the module: [its template](./templates/google-group-unit) renders a Terragrunt unit. **Generate** writes it under `google-groups/` in the clone.

## Push it

Nothing is applied that isn't pushed, so the pull request comes first.

<GitHubPullRequest
  id="pr"
  githubAuthId="github"
  prefilledPullRequestTitle="Add the {{ .inputs.id }} Google group"
  inputsId="group"
/>

## Apply it

<TerragruntApply id="apply-group" path="{{ .outputs.group.CODE_PATH }}" auth={["workspace"]} />

Plan first runs the module's preflight checks through the `workspace` block, then shows what the plan would create. Once it applies, the module's outputs are this block's outputs, such as `{{ .outputs.apply_group.runbooks_console_url }}`.

## Use the values

Other blocks read the module's inputs through `inputsId`, as they read an `<Inputs>` block's.

<Command
  id="show-group"
  title="Show the group's inputs"
  inputsId="group"
  env={{
    GROUP_EMAIL: "{{ .inputs.id }}",
    GROUP_NAME: "{{ .inputs.display_name }}",
    GROUP_DOMAIN: "{{ .inputs.domain }}",
  }}
  command={`echo "Group:  $GROUP_EMAIL"
echo "Name:   $GROUP_NAME"
echo "Domain: $GROUP_DOMAIN"
echo "group_email=$GROUP_EMAIL" >> "$RUNBOOK_OUTPUT"`}
/>
